@@ -0,0 +1,229 @@
+# ◈ GALACTIC NEWS DISPATCH ◈
+
+## Deep Space Signal Intercept — Patch Bulletin v0.2.0 → v0.3.0
+
+**FleetComms ID:** `RELEASE-v0.3.0-alpha.1`
+**Encryption:** Public
+**Distribution:** All Terminals
+
+---
+
+### SIGNAL SUMMARY
+
+FARSPACE Command reports 48 verified dispatches across 99 stellar chart
+revisions between v0.2.0-alpha and v0.3.0-alpha.1. Net throughput:
+**11,555 lines inserted, 2,920 removed** — the largest sustained
+engineering campaign since first contact.
+
+Four signal sources identified:
+`lgulliver` (Command), `copilot-swe-agent[bot]` (Automated TUI Corps),
+`dependabot[bot]` (Supply Logistics), `Liam Gulliver` (Command, alternate
+transmission band).
+
+---
+
+## [»] STRATEGIC COMMAND — Sector Governance & Automation v1
+
+*Severity: Notable*
+
+Governors now take orders. The Sector Governance screen (`G`) introduces
+per-sector strategic directives and sector-guided build automation — a
+framework for delegating local production decisions without surrendering
+strategic control.
+
+- **Directive system:** Cycle directives per sector (`D`) — Develop,
+  Fortify, Reclaim, Science Focus, and balanced presets guide AI build
+  recommendations at the sector level.
+- **Sector-guided automation:** Toggle automation (`A`) to let the
+  directive engine queue colony builds; manual override still available.
+- **Last-turn output reporting:** Each sector reports what was built
+  last turn, so automation never becomes a black box.
+- **Yield preview:** Sector production, food, science, and credit
+  estimates account for directive modifiers.
+- **Codex review addressed:** Palette layout corrections and accurate
+  sector yield calculations applied post-review.
+
+**Files affected:** 27 files, ~1,870 insertions
+**Key modules:** `sector_governance.rs` (new TUI screen), `engine.rs`,
+`commands.rs`, `state.rs` (core governance state & validation),
+`events.rs` (governance event variants)
+
+---
+
+## [»] ARCHIVAL RECORDS — Campaign Archives Save Browser
+
+*Severity: Notable*
+
+The Campaign Archives system introduces a dedicated save browser
+accessible from the main menu and the `:save` / `:load` command palette.
+Players can now browse, inspect metadata, and load campaign histories
+without navigating blind.
+
+- **Save browser UI:** Full-screen archive viewer with per-save metadata
+  (empire, turn count, galaxy age).
+- **Continue flow:** Direct "Continue" path from menu jumps to the most
+  recent active campaign.
+- **Metadata API:** Save timestamps, version info, and campaign summary
+  surfaced in the browser.
+- **Persistence:** Backed by the game_save crate's versioned schema
+  (CURRENT_VERSION = 36).
+
+**Files:** `archives.rs` (500-line TUI screen), `app.rs` (navigation &
+state), `game_save/src/lib.rs` (metadata API)
+
+---
+
+## [»] ADVISORY CORPS — Deterministic Advisor Guidance
+
+*Severity: Notable*
+
+The Advisor system is now wired into the TUI as a persistent overlay,
+providing deterministic, context-aware counsel across economy,
+diplomacy, research, and tutorial domains.
+
+- **Advisor component:** 345-line dedicated TUI widget renders advice
+  based on current game state — no RNG, no hidden heuristics.
+- **Economy advisor:** Flags deficits, supply disruptions, production
+  inefficiencies.
+- **Diplomacy advisor:** Surfaces stance shifts, relationship drift,
+  intel gaps.
+- **Tutorial guidance:** Contextual onboarding nudges for new players.
+- **Deterministic output:** Same state → same advice, guaranteed.
+
+**Files:** `components/advisor.rs`, `screens/sector_overview.rs`,
+`app.rs` (wiring)
+
+---
+
+## [·] INTERFACE — Screen Transition Scaffolding & UI Animation Utils
+
+*Severity: Notice*
+
+A new deterministic animation module (`animation.rs`) provides shared
+scaffolding for screen transitions. Includes easing curves, frame
+timing, and composable transition states — all seeded from game state,
+never from wall-clock time.
+
+- **Animation primitives:** `Easing` enum (Linear, EaseIn, EaseOut,
+  EaseInOut), `TransitionState`, composable frame producers.
+- **Zero RNG:** All transitions are fully deterministic — replay-safe
+  by construction.
+- **Integration hooks:** `app.rs` accepts animation state for future
+  screen fade, slide, and crossfade effects.
+
+**Files:** `animation.rs` (new), `app.rs`, `app/tests.rs`
+
+---
+
+## [★★] VISUAL IDENTITY — TUI Foundation Program
+
+*Severity: Historic*
+
+A comprehensive TUI visual overhaul across the entire surface. This is
+the single largest UX change in the v0.3.0 cycle — touching every
+screen, component, and theme file in the terminal layer.
+
+### Foundation Primitives
+
+- **Shared chrome module:** Unified border, titlebar, and panel
+  rendering with splash-screen-grade layout.
+- **Footer system:** Consistent contextual key hints and status bar
+  across all screens.
+- **Header component:** Standardised screen title block with optional
+  metadata line.
+- **Meter component:** Optimised display-width calculations for
+  resource bars — no more overflow or clipping at narrow terminal widths.
+
+### Screen Refresh (Pass 1–3 Campaign)
+
+- **Splash chrome** applied to Sector Map, Sector Overview, and System
+  screens — the three most-frequented tactical views.
+- **Strategic Map & Overview:** Full chrome and layout refresh with
+  consistent spacing, metre alignment, and information hierarchy.
+  Sector map gains resizable side-panel and fleet-count indicators.
+- **Management Screens:** Colony layout rebuilt (562→ lines rewritten),
+  Empire Overview restructured (376→ lines), Research queue view
+  expanded, Ship Designer interface reflowed.
+- **Diplomacy Screen:** Relationship state display, intel level
+  indicators, faction profile rendering — all rebuilt with palette
+  consistency.
+- **Settings Screen:** Refactored into a themed modal overlay with
+  category grouping and live preview.
+- **Empire Select:** Streamlined faction picker with emblem rendering,
+  trait summary, and palette-adjusted colour swatches.
+- **Help Screen:** Consolidated key reference with category grouping.
+- **New Game Wizard:** 860-line expansion — emblem display, galaxy
+  size visualisation, seed input with randomise option.
+
+### Style Guide & Theme System
+
+- **TUI Style Guide:** New canonical reference document
+  (`docs/design/tui-style-guide.md`) defining spacing, colour roles,
+  typography, and composition standards for all future screens.
+- **Theme `mod.rs` refactored:** Palette roles extracted into
+  `theme/palette.rs`; capability detection moved to
+  `theme/capability.rs`; gradient support in `theme/gradient.rs`.
+- **Accessibility pass:** Tests verify minimum contrast ratios across
+  all palette roles (light and dark visual modes). Emblem rendering
+  includes foreground-colour-aware fallbacks.
+- **Visual Mode support:** All refreshed screens respect
+  ASCII/Unicode/Nerd Font modes.
+
+---
+
+## [»] RESEARCH & ECONOMICS — Edge-Case Tightening
+
+*Severity: Notable*
+
+The yield model and research progression received a focused math
+correction pass:
+
+- **Meter display-width optimisation:** Unicode-aware width
+  calculation prevents bar overflow in mixed-width terminal
+  environments. New `unicode-width` dependency.
+- **Research edge-case math:** Redundant progress allocation at tech
+  completion, research overflow carry, and zero-cost tech boundary
+  conditions all corrected.
+- **Meter math re-tightened:** Fractional-bar rounding now guarantees
+  100% fill at max without overshoot — reapplied after a revert cycle
+  that validated the fix independently.
+
+---
+
+## [·] INFRASTRUCTURE — Dependencies & Tooling
+
+*Severity: Notice*
+
+- **ratatui** upgraded 0.29.0 → 0.30.0: API improvements in frame
+  rendering, constraint layout, and style system. Required minor
+  compatibility changes across 4 game_tui files.
+- **crossterm** upgraded 0.28.1 → 0.29.0: Terminal event handling and
+  resize improvements.
+- **ureq** upgraded 2.12.1 → 3.3.0: HTTP client updated to new
+  blocking API; update-checker module refactored accordingly.
+- **thiserror** upgraded 1.0.69 → 2.0.18: Error derive macro
+  improvements (trait bounds, `#[error(...)]` syntax).
+- **serde_json** upgraded 1.0.149 → 1.0.150: Maintenance release.
+- **Rust edition** bumped from 2021 → 2024: All 63 workspace crates
+  migrated with required lifetime, trait, and syntax adjustments.
+  Use of `unsafe` blocks reduced. Edition 2024's `unsafe_fields`,
+  `unsafe_attr_outside_unsafe`, and `gen` keyword migration applied.
+- **dependabot** configured for Cargo ecosystem (`.github/dependabot.yml`).
+- **pullfrog.yml** workflow added for automated PR management.
+
+---
+
+## [·] COMMAND SIGN-OFF
+
+*Severity: Notice*
+
+```
+Archive:  docs/releases/v0.3.0.md
+Status:   TRANSMITTED
+From:     FARSPACE Development Command
+Channel:  Galactic News Dispatch — Release Bulletin
+```
+
+Full changelog: `git log v0.2.0-alpha..v0.3.0-alpha.1`
+
+**4 contributors, 48 dispatches, 99 sectors charted.**

Use `rand::SeedableRng`. - **Never** seed from `SystemTime`, `Instant`, or any other wall-clock or OS source. - **Never** iterate `HashMap` without sorting keys first — use `BTreeMap` for ordered collections or sort before use. - Simulation must be fully reproducible: same seed + same commands ⇒ same output. - Tests for deterministic systems must use fixed seeds and assert exact output. --- ## Coding Conventions - Prefer small, focused modules. - Use strongly-typed ID newtypes (`StarId(u64)`, `EmpireId(u64)`, `FleetId(u64)`) — never bare integers. - Use enums for `Command` and `Event` — no stringly-typed dispatch. - Return `Vec` from `apply_turn`; surface validation failures as `Event::Error`. - Add a test for every meaningful change. - Tests must include at least one positive path and one negative/error path. - When adding a new command: add enum variant, validation arm in `apply_turn`, event emission, and tests. --- ## Feature Scope — Do Not Add Without Explicit Request Do not add any of the following unless the issue/task explicitly asks for it: - Tactical (hex/grid) combat - Multiplayer or networked play - Deep diplomacy systems (trade routes, alliances, treaties) - Complex AI beyond basic expansion/defence - Any content copied from Master of Orion: no faction names, ship names, tech names, planet names, numbers, or text from that series --- ## Original IP Policy FARSPACE uses original content only. Phases are ordered delivery slices from current alpha to shippable v1 and expansion.

Status labels:

- **Done**
- **In Progress**
- **Planned**

---

## Phase 0 — Foundation

**Goal:** stable workspace, CI gates, deterministic command/event core, save/load base.

**Current status:** **Done**

**Key deliverables:**

- Workspace crate split (`game_core`, `game_tui`, `game_content`, `game_save`, `farspace`)
- CI gates (`fmt`, `clippy`, `test`, coverage)
- Deterministic command/event simulation baseline
- Versioned save/load with migration path

**Dependencies:** none (base layer)

**Risks:** low; drift risk if boundaries are not enforced in future slices

**Acceptance criteria:** CI green, deterministic tests present, save round-trip and migration tests present

---

## Phase 1 — Playable Core Loop

**Goal:** playable early loop through exploration, colonization, economy, research, and turn progression.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Galaxy generation
- Main menu + new game setup
- Galaxy/sector navigation and system selection
- Colony basics and end-turn pipeline
- Event log as turn feedback channel

**Dependencies:** Phase 0 foundation

**Risks:** UX discoverability, imbalance in early pacing

**Acceptance criteria:** player can run full multi-turn loop without debug tools; no deterministic regressions

---

## Phase 2 — Exploration & Spatial Galaxy

**Goal:** deepen map traversal and scouting/survey flow with spatial travel constraints.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Science ships and planet survey flow
- System view and sector navigation polish
- Distance-based travel timings
- Fleet movement visualization in map contexts
- Hyperspace lane generation and lane-aware travel behavior

**Dependencies:** Phase 1 loop stability

**Risks:** readability in dense sectors, pathing edge cases, movement clarity in TUI

**Acceptance criteria:** exploration/survey/travel loops are clear, deterministic, and test-covered

---

## Phase 3 — Colony Economy

**Goal:** evolve colonies from queue-only nodes into strategic economic systems.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Planet class/size/slot effects
- Orbital infrastructure and shipyards
- Population/food/housing/growth fundamentals
- Yield model refinement and maintenance/supply pressure
- Pop/jobs-lite baseline
- Colony roles and role-driven modifiers

**Dependencies:** Phases 1-2

**Risks:** economy snowballing, maintenance deadlocks, UI complexity

**Acceptance criteria:** economy remains legible, deterministic, and recoverable from deficit states

---

## Phase 4 — Research & Progression

**Goal:** robust progression pacing via broad tech tree and queue-driven planning.

**Current status:** **In Progress** (Tech Tree v2 and Research Queue complete)

**Key deliverables:**

- ✅ Large-Scale technology tree
- ✅ Research queue management
- Unlock integration (ships/buildings/capabilities)
- Rare/future-hook technologies with clear signaling
- AI research weighting aligned with faction profiles

**Dependencies:** Phase 3 economy maturity

**Risks:** tech bloat without gameplay payoff, AI mismatch to unlocks

**Acceptance criteria:** research choices are meaningful and unlock effects are mechanically visible

---

## Phase 5 — Fleets, Shipyards & Combat

**Goal:** complete strategic fleet warfare loop in deterministic auto-resolve model.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Ship production from colony/shipyard systems
- Expanded ship archetype roster
- Auto-resolve combat outcomes and reporting
- Blockades and orbital defense interactions
- Invasion and troop transport strategic layer

**Dependencies:** Phases 2-4

**Risks:** combat readability, invasion balance, maintenance pressure

**Acceptance criteria:** fleet combat/invasion outcomes are deterministic, explainable, and test-covered

**Goal:** richer multi-empire strategy through identity, planning, and diplomacy state.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Empire selection and identity effects
- Faction identity depth (major + future minor faction hooks)
- AI planning and doctrine behavior
- Diplomacy relation bands and war state behavior
- Trade/supply strategic coupling

**Dependencies:** Phases 3-5

**Risks:** AI transparency, diplomacy complexity vs current UI affordances

**Acceptance criteria:** empire identity affects play, AI behavior is coherent, diplomacy state changes are visible and deterministic

---

## Phase 7 — Strategic Management & UX

**Goal:** reduce command friction and improve strategic observability.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Empire overview management workflows
- Turn report/notification quality improvements
- Rally points and fleet order usability
- Command palette polish
- Help/search/filtering improvements across screens

**Dependencies:** Phase 6 state richness

**Risks:** input overload, inconsistent key flows, signal-to-noise in logs

**Acceptance criteria:** common strategic tasks are fast to execute and understandable from UI feedback

---

**Goal:** define session completion and post-session outcomes.

**Current status:** **Planned**

**Key deliverables:**

- Victory conditions and trigger rules
- Scenario setup options and presets
- Scoring framework
- Campaign summary outputs
- Replay log + determinism audit tooling

**Dependencies:** stable core loops from phases 1-7

**Risks:** premature end-state rules before balance maturity

**Acceptance criteria:** players can complete a run and get clear outcome summary

**Current status:** **Planned**

- Terraforming systems
- Advanced diplomacy (alliances/federations)
- Megaprojects and precursor ruins
- Dynamic events and crisis systems
- Advanced logistics and supply complexity

**Dependencies:** phase 8 end-state foundation

**Risks:** scope growth, readability cost, determinism stress in complex interactions

**Acceptance criteria:** late game remains deterministic, comprehensible, and performance-safe

---

## Phase 10 — Release Hardening

**Goal:** ship-quality reliability, compatibility, and maintainability.

**Current status:** **Planned**

**Key deliverables:**

- Save migration hardening
- Performance benchmarks and optimization pass
- Accessibility and low-motion UX pass
- Cross-platform packaging and terminal compatibility matrix
- Balance pass and playtest/manual documentation

**Dependencies:** phases 1-9 feature stability

**Risks:** regressions from hardening changes, platform variance

**Acceptance criteria:** stable release candidate with green CI, migration confidence, and validated compatibility targets

**Dependencies:** Phase 0 foundation

**Risks:** UX discoverability, imbalance in early pacing

**Acceptance criteria:** player can run full multi-turn loop without debug tools; no deterministic regressions

---

## Phase 2 — Exploration & Spatial Galaxy

**Goal:** deepen map traversal and scouting/survey flow with spatial travel constraints.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Science ships and planet survey flow
- System view and sector navigation polish
- Distance-based travel timings
- Fleet movement visualization in map contexts
- Hyperspace lane generation and lane-aware travel behavior

**Dependencies:** Phase 1 loop stability

**Risks:** readability in dense sectors, pathing edge cases, movement clarity in TUI

**Acceptance criteria:** exploration/survey/travel loops are clear, deterministic, and test-covered

---

## Phase 3 — Colony Economy

**Goal:** evolve colonies from queue-only nodes into strategic economic systems.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Planet class/size/slot effects
- Orbital infrastructure and shipyards
- Population/food/housing/growth fundamentals
- Yield model refinement and maintenance/supply pressure
- Pop/jobs-lite baseline
- Colony roles and role-driven modifiers

**Dependencies:** Phases 1-2

**Risks:** economy snowballing, maintenance deadlocks, UI complexity

**Acceptance criteria:** economy remains legible, deterministic, and recoverable from deficit states

---

## Phase 4 — Research & Progression

**Goal:** robust progression pacing via broad tech tree and queue-driven planning.

**Current status:** **In Progress** (Tech Tree v2 and Research Queue complete)

**Key deliverables:**

- ✅ Large-Scale technology tree
- ✅ Research queue management
- Unlock integration (ships/buildings/capabilities)
- Rare/future-hook technologies with clear signaling
- AI research weighting aligned with faction profiles

**Dependencies:** Phase 3 economy maturity

**Risks:** tech bloat without gameplay payoff, AI mismatch to unlocks

**Acceptance criteria:** research choices are meaningful and unlock effects are mechanically visible

---

## Phase 5 — Fleets, Shipyards & Combat

**Goal:** complete strategic fleet warfare loop in deterministic auto-resolve model.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Ship production from colony/shipyard systems
- Expanded ship archetype roster
- Auto-resolve combat outcomes and reporting
- Blockades and orbital defense interactions
- Invasion and troop transport strategic layer

**Dependencies:** Phases 2-4

**Risks:** combat readability, invasion balance, maintenance pressure

**Acceptance criteria:** fleet combat/invasion outcomes are deterministic, explainable, and test-covered

---

## Phase 6 — Empires, AI & Diplomacy

**Goal:** richer multi-empire strategy through identity, planning, and diplomacy state.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Empire selection and identity effects
- Faction identity depth (major + future minor faction hooks)
- AI planning and doctrine behavior
- Diplomacy relation bands and war state behavior
- Trade/supply strategic coupling

**Dependencies:** Phases 3-5

**Risks:** AI transparency, diplomacy complexity vs current UI affordances

**Acceptance criteria:** empire identity affects play, AI behavior is coherent, diplomacy state changes are visible and deterministic

---

## Phase 7 — Strategic Management & UX

**Goal:** reduce command friction and improve strategic observability.

**Current status:** **In Progress**

**Key deliverables:**

- Empire overview management workflows
- Turn report/notification quality improvements
- Rally points and fleet order usability
- Command palette polish
- Help/search/filtering improvements across screens

**Dependencies:** Phase 6 state richness

**Risks:** input overload, inconsistent key flows, signal-to-noise in logs

**Acceptance criteria:** common strategic tasks are fast to execute and understandable from UI feedback

---

## Phase 8 — Victory & Campaign Structure

**Goal:** define session completion and post-session outcomes.

**Current status:** **Planned**

**Key deliverables:**

- Victory conditions and trigger rules
- Scenario setup options and presets
- Scoring framework
- Campaign summary outputs
- Replay log + determinism audit tooling

**Dependencies:** stable core loops from phases 1-7

**Risks:** premature end-state rules before balance maturity

**Acceptance criteria:** players can complete a run and get clear outcome summary

---

## Phase 9 — Late Game Expansion

**Goal:** add high-depth strategic systems for long-form campaigns.

**Current status:** **Planned**

**Key deliverables:**

- Terraforming systems
- Advanced diplomacy (alliances/federations)
- Megaprojects and precursor ruins
- Dynamic events and crisis systems
- Advanced logistics and supply complexity

**Dependencies:** phase 8 end-state foundation

**Risks:** scope growth, readability cost, determinism stress in complex interactions

**Acceptance criteria:** late game remains deterministic, comprehensible, and performance-safe

---

## Phase 10 — Release Hardening

**Goal:** ship-quality reliability, compatibility, and maintainability.

**Current status:** **Planned**

**Key deliverables:**

- Save migration hardening
- Performance benchmarks and optimization pass
- Accessibility and low-motion UX pass
- Cross-platform packaging and terminal compatibility matrix
- Balance pass and playtest/manual documentation

**Dependencies:** phases 1-9 feature stability

**Risks:** regressions from hardening changes, platform variance

**Acceptance criteria:** stable release candidate with green CI, migration confidence, and validated compatibility targets

Now I have a clear picture of what changed between v0.2.0-alpha and v0.3.0-alpha.1. Let me also check if there's a CHANGELOG or any existing release notes format.

Key features between v0.2.0-alpha and v0.3.0-alpha.1:

1. **Sector Governance & Automation v1** - major feature: per-sector strategic directives and guided build automation, with `G` key binding, sector governance screen (425 lines in governance screen alone)
2. **Campaign Archives** - save browser and Continue flow
3. **Advisor Guidance** - deterministic advisor wired into TUI
4. **TUI Animation Utils** - screen-transition scaffolding
5. **TUI Consistency pass** - style guide, theme roles, accessibility
6. **Screen Refreshes**: 
   - Diplomacy, Settings, Help, Empire Select screens refreshed
   - Strategic Map and Overview screens polished with chrome
   - Management screens (Colony, Empire Overview, Research, Ship Designer) refreshed

1: # Galactic Dispatch
2: 
3: Galactic Dispatch is a recurring in-universe news bulletin that surfaces important galaxy-wide events in an atmospheric, flavourful way. It improves strategic readability and game atmosphere without leaking hidden information or mutating game state.
4: 
5: ---
6: 
7: ## Feature Name
8: 
9: **Galactic Dispatch** — an in-universe signal intercept / intelligence briefing. Not modelled on any existing 4X franchise; all names, headlines, and presentation are original.
10: 
11: ---
12: 
13: ## Cadence
14: 
15: | Constant | Value | Meaning |
16: |---|---|---|
17: | `DISPATCH_CADENCE` | 5 | A dispatch is always generated every 5 turns |
18: | `DISPATCH_MAX_HISTORY` | 10 | At most 10 recent dispatches are retained in `GameState.galactic_dispatches` |
19: 
20: A dispatch is generated when `completed_turn % DISPATCH_CADENCE == 0`, where `completed_turn` is the value of `GameState::turn` **before** it is incremented. Because normal games start at `turn = 1`, the first in-game cadence dispatch is emitted when `state.turn` advances to a multiple of `DISPATCH_CADENCE + 1` (i.e. turns 5, 10, 15, …). The `completed_turn = 0` cadence used in unit tests reflects an initial state that starts before the first real game turn.
21: 
22: Off-cadence dispatches are only generated when at least one **Urgent** or **Historic** item is present (e.g. a blockade, invasion, or victory achievement).
23: 
24: ---
25: 
26: ## Data Model
27: 
28: ```
29: GalacticDispatch
30:   turn: u32                  — completed turn when the dispatch was generated
31:   title: String              — display title ("Galactic Dispatch — Turn N")
32:   items: Vec<DispatchItem>   — sorted, stable-ordered items
33: 
34: DispatchItem
35:   category: DispatchCategory
36:   severity: DispatchSeverity
37:   headline: String           — concise, atmospheric, original
38:   body: String               — one or two sentence expansion
39:   related_empire_id: Option<EmpireId>
40:   related_star_id: Option<StarId>
41:   related_planet_index: Option<usize>
42: ```
43: 
44: ---
45: 
46: ## Categories
47: 
48: | Variant | Covers |
49: |---|---|
50: | `Exploration` | System exploration, orbital surveys |
51: | `Colonization` | Colony founding (player and AI) |
52: | `Research` | Technology breakthroughs, research redirections |
53: | `Economy` | Credit deficits, food shortages |
54: | `Diplomacy` | First contact, relationship shifts |
55: | `War` | Fleet combat outcomes |
56: | `Blockades` | Blockade starts |
57: | `Invasions` | Planetary invasions (success and failure) |
58: | `Trade` | Colony isolation / supply network disruption |
59: | `VictoryRace` | Victory-path progress milestones, winner |
60: | `MinorFactions` | Reserved for future minor faction contacts |
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ## Severity Levels
65: 
66: | Variant | Marker | Style | When used |
67: |---|---|---|---|
68: | `Notice` | `[·]` | Muted | Routine exploration, AI research redirections |
69: | `Notable` | `[»]` | Title | Colonization, first contact, minor war, food shortage |
70: | `Urgent` | `[!!]` | Error (red) | Blockades, credit deficit, invasion attempts |
71: | `Historic` | `[★★]` | Accent | Ancient ruins, high-progress victory milestones (≥80 %), victories, invasion conquests |
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## Generation Sources
76: 
77: The dispatch is derived from the event stream emitted during `process_end_turn`. The following `Event` variants map to dispatch items:
78: 
79: | Event | Category | Severity |
80: |---|---|---|
81: | `SystemExplored` | Exploration | Notice |
82: | `PlanetSurveyCompleted` | Exploration | Notice |
83: | `AncientRuinsDiscovered` | Research | Historic |
84: | `ColonizationCompleted` | Colonization | Notable |
85: | `AiColonized` | Colonization | Notable (or vague if empire unknown) |
86: | `ResearchCompleted` (player) | Research | Notable |
87: | `AiResearchSelected` | Research | Notice (if empire known) |
88: | `CombatResolved` | War | Urgent/Notable depending on player involvement |
89: | `BlockadeStarted` | Blockades | Urgent |
90: | `InvasionSucceeded` | Invasions | Historic |
91: | `InvasionFailed` | Invasions | Notable |
92: | `FoodShortage` (player) | Economy | Urgent |
93: | `EconomySummary` with deficit (player) | Economy | Notable |
94: | `ColonyIsolated` (player colony) | Trade | Notable |
95: | `FirstContact` | Diplomacy | Notable |
96: | `VictoryProgressMilestone` | VictoryRace | Notable (or Historic if ≥80 %) |
97: | `VictoryAchieved` | VictoryRace | Historic |
98: 
99: Dispatches do not generate random events — they only reflect what actually happened this turn.
100: 
101: ---
102: 
103: ## Public Information Rules
104: 
105: Dispatch content is filtered to avoid leaking hidden state:
106: 
107: 1. **Unknown empires**: if the player has not made contact with an empire (`RelationshipStatus::Unknown` or absent from `diplomacy`), that empire's name and ID are withheld. Vague wording is used instead:
108:    - "Unknown Forces Establish Remote Colony"
109:    - "Unidentified Fleet Engages Forces Near [star]"
110:    - "Unidentified Fleet Blockades Contested Colony"
111: 
112: 2. **Unsurveyed planets**: planet specials and strategic resources are never referenced in dispatch text until the planet has been surveyed.
113: 
114: 3. **Unseen stars**: system exploration events are only surfaced when the player's own fleet explored them (event is already player-scoped). AI-explored stars are not reported as exploration events.
115: 
116: 4. **AI combat**: if the player is not involved in combat and neither fleet's empire is known, the combat event is skipped entirely.
117: 
118: ---
119: 
120: ## Item Ordering (Determinism)
121: 
122: Items are sorted by a composite key:
123: 
124: 1. Severity descending (Historic → Urgent → Notable → Notice)
125: 2. Category ascending (enum declaration order, mapped to u8)
126: 3. Headline ascending (lexicographic)
127: 
128: This produces a stable, deterministic order regardless of event insertion order or BTreeMap iteration. Same events + same state always produce identical dispatch output.
129: 
130: ---
131: 
132: ## Deduplication
133: 
134: Multiple events of the same type in one turn are collapsed:
135: - Multiple `SystemExplored` events → one Exploration item ("Survey Crews Chart New Frontier Worlds")
136: - Multiple `PlanetSurveyCompleted` events → one Exploration item
137: 
138: This is achieved via a `BTreeSet<(DispatchCategory, String)>` deduplication set.
139: 
140: ---
141: 
142: ## Examples
143: 
144: ```
145: ╔══════════════════════════════════════════╗
146: ║       ◈ GALACTIC DISPATCH ◈              ║
147: ║  Turn 5  ·  Dispatch 1/1                 ║
148: ║──────────────────────────────────────────║
149: ║ [★★] [RESEARCH]                          ║
150: ║  Ancient Ruins Discovered —              ║
151: ║  Archaeological Teams Mobilize           ║
152: ║   Excavations begun at Keth Prime.       ║
153: ║                                          ║
154: ║ [»]  [COLONIZATION]                      ║
155: ║  Colonists Establish Foothold in         ║
156: ║  Vela System                             ║
157: ║   A colonial charter has been issued     ║
158: ║   for Vela II.                           ║
159: ║──────────────────────────────────────────║
160: ║  ← prev / → next   Esc to close         ║
161: ╚══════════════════════════════════════════╝
162: ```
163: 
164: ---
165: 
166: ## TUI Interaction
167: 
168: | Key / Command | Action |
169: |---|---|
170: | `N` (global, in-game) | Open latest Galactic Dispatch |
171: | `:dispatch` | Open latest Galactic Dispatch |
172: | `:news` | Alias for `:dispatch` |
173: | `←` / `h` | Cycle to previous dispatch in history |
174: | `→` / `l` | Cycle to next dispatch in history |
175: | `Esc` / `N` / `n` | Close dispatch overlay |
176: 
177: The dispatch overlay is shown automatically when a new dispatch is generated at the end of a turn.
178: 
179: ---
180: 
181: ## Persistence (Save/Load)
182: 
183: `galactic_dispatches` is stored in `GameState` as a `VecDeque<GalacticDispatch>`. It is serialised via serde (behind the `serde` feature flag on `game_core`). Old saves (schema ≤ 28) load with an empty history via `#[serde(default)]`.
184: 
185: Save schema version: **29** (introduced with Galactic Dispatch v1).
186: 
187: ---
188: 
189: ## Determinism and Replay
190: 
191: - `generate_dispatch` takes only `completed_turn`, the event slice, and a shared reference to `GameState`. It uses no RNG and no wall-clock logic.
192: - Same seed + same command log → same events → same dispatches.
193: - `galactic_dispatches` is included in `GameState`'s manual `PartialEq` implementation, so equality checks (e.g. in save-load round-trip tests) compare dispatch history along with all other game state.
194: 
195: ---
196: 
197: ## Future Hooks
198: 
199: - **Minor faction sightings**: `MinorFactions` category is reserved for when minor independent factions are introduced.
200: - **Reduced-interruptions mode**: a future `reduced_interruptions` flag in UI settings can suppress automatic dispatch opening.
201: - **Dispatch filtering by category**: the TUI modal could gain a category filter.
202: - **Clickable context links**: headlines with `related_star_id` could eventually jump to that system.
203: - **Urgent off-cadence dispatch**: the off-cadence Urgent/Historic rule is already implemented; future "galactic crisis" events can piggyback on it.

(End of file - total 203 lines)
</content>
